name: inline-edit
title: Inline Edit
description: Text you rename in place: it becomes a field without moving, an underline draws in, and a check confirms the save.

perf.budget: One native text input while editing and two shared values; the icons are 16 pt Skia paths. Nothing runs at rest.

measurements.notes: p99 spikes are the keyboard opening when editing starts.

a11y.reducedMotion: The underline and buttons appear without a spring; the check still fades.
a11y.screenReader: A button that reads the label and the value; while editing, a text field plus Cancel and Save buttons.
a11y.touchTarget: The text and both buttons are at least 44 pt tall.

meta.guide:
## Usage

```tsx
import { InlineEdit } from '@/components/kinetik/inline-edit';

<InlineEdit accessibilityLabel="Project name" value={name} onSubmit={setName} />;
```

## When to use

- Names and titles people rename now and then: a project, a playlist, a board.
- Detail screens where a separate edit form would be heavier than the change.

## When not to use

- Several related fields that should be saved together. Use a form with one Save button.
- Text that needs validation with an explanation. Use Float Field, which has room for an error.

## Notes

- The label and the field share `textStyle`, so the text does not move when editing starts.
- Return or Save keeps the trimmed text, Cancel restores the old one, and leaving the field saves it. An empty edit is dropped.
- Inside a `ScrollView`, set `keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"` so the buttons work while the keyboard is open.

docs: Prefer `npx kinetik-ui add inline-edit`: it installs dependencies with expo install, so versions match your Expo SDK.
